root_cause.summary: The old 60-second loop invoked deploy.sh for all 20 projects before checking whether anything changed. Each invocation did a Git/SSH fetch; 20 projects share 14 repos. It also ran a two-SSH subdomain audit on every unchanged admin check.
root_cause.idle_evidence: All 20 deployed SHAs matched live remote main heads; both before windows contained no builds, successful deployments, or failed builds. Sampled child processes included git fetch and ssh git-upload-pack.

historical_audit.comparison_note: Historical shorter (~35s) sample is retained. The new controlled before/after comparisons below use 120s unchanged-source windows; short samples can weight the active fetch phase differently.

fix.normal_path: One authenticated GraphQL query for all unique GitHub repos per cycle. Persist the HTTP client and reconnect a stale connection before using Git fallback. No recurring Git/SSH/fetch/build processes while unchanged.
unchanged_features: Existing webhook service and deployment endpoints
deploy.sh fetch/archive/build/deploy path, including existing local adapter
State-file based retry and forced redeploy by deleting a state file
fix.recovery: Missing API access/auth or non-GitHub repos use git ls-remote once per unique repo. Missing remote results do not deploy stale refs. Failed/busy deployments stay pending. Refreshed tokens, reconnects, and partial API access are retried.
fix.subdomain_audit: Run only after a successful admin state change.
fix.shutdown: Release the watcher lifetime flock and do not launch another pending deployment after stop is requested.

files_changed.change: Keep the existing project list and interval; exec the Python metadata watcher.
One GraphQL head batch per 60-second cycle, blocking wait, SHA gating, grouped Git fallback, reconnects, watcher flock, and shutdown handling.
Add --watch-config to expose repo/state paths; existing fetch/build/deploy path unchanged.
11 safe regression checks using temporary Git remotes and fake deploy handlers.
Document normal checks, fallback, trigger behavior, and safe regression command.

checks: Remote main push detected even with stale local origin/main; unchanged cycles start no fake deployments
Shared repo triggers all relevant fixture projects once
Failed build retries without acknowledging SHA
Missing remote head never triggers from stale data
Deleting state forces redeploy; subdomain audit only follows an actual admin change
No Git commands on normal unchanged cycles after startup config discovery
API failure falls back and recovers; partial access uses Git only for unavailable repo
Expired HTTP keep-alive reconnects; unauthorized token is reloaded
Shutdown does not start the next pending build
A duplicate watcher exits without interfering with the running service

method.includes: all service processes and child work, including subprocesses that exit between snapshots
method.normalization: one logical CPU; 100% = one logical CPU saturated
method.limits: cpu.stat is exposed in microsecond units; process snapshots can miss short-lived processes but CPU deltas include their CPU. Idle windows exclude initial startup and actual builds. Values below 0.05% round to 0.0% at one decimal; they are not mathematical zero.

measurements.workload: Unchanged remote main/deployed SHAs; no real builds/deployments in either before or after windows. Each 120s window exceeds the former ~95s fetch-plus-sleep cycle and includes at least two new 60s head checks.
limits: Near-zero is measured idle CPU, not mathematical zero. Both final intervals round to 0.0% at one decimal.
Cold startup, real builds, and Git fallback during API/auth failures consume CPU and are outside this normal idle comparison.
Process snapshots are descriptive; all CPU calculations use inclusive cgroup counters.

preservation.preexisting_local_changes: Preserved exactly and left unstaged: README repo symlink example, project/repo config additions, local deploy adapter, watcher events entry, blog autopush and webhook edits. Only this task's implementation was committed.
preservation.unit_and_launcher: Unchanged; restart only veron3-deploy.service twice to load implementation and final shutdown fix.

rollback.minimal_functional: Inspect/merge any later watcher.sh edits, restore the preserved pre-fix deploy/watcher.sh, then restart only veron3-deploy.service. The extra deploy.sh config mode and unused Python file do not change the old normal deploy path.
